text:
A: Hiya! Gary, is it? I'm Ryan. Long Eaton, between Derby and Nottingham. How you doing?
B: Alright. Dagenham.
A: Dagenham, brilliant. Is that a West Ham cushion I saw in your photo?
B: Yeah.
A: I'm Derby, so I'm not in a position to laugh at anyone. We lost again Saturday. I think I'm just a glutton for punishment at this point.
B: At least you've got a proper ground. We got moved to that soulless bowl. Gave up my season ticket over it. Thirty-odd years at Upton Park, then they stick you in a running track with a roof.
A: Oh, that's grim. Upton Park was a proper ground, though. My dad took me there once, actually, we lost two-nil and he still said it was one of the best atmospheres he'd been in.
B: It was. Gone now. Flats.
A: Flats. Course it is. Sorry, I'm a history teacher, so I get really sad about that sort of thing. Old grounds, old factories.
B: Thought you was a teacher.
A: Is it the lanyard? It's always the lanyard. What do you do, Gary?
B: Office at a skip firm. Rainham. Phones, booking skips, chasing money.
A: Chasing money. I bet you're good at that.
B: I don't let 'em off, put it that way. They say the cheque's in the post, I ring every day till it is.
A: Ha! I should get you to chase my Year 9 homework. Half of them have owed me an essay since September.
B: Same thing really. Just younger.
A: Just younger, ha! Was that your son in the graduation photo behind you?
B: Yeah. Liam. Did a course at college, business or summat. Moved to Romford with his girlfriend.
A: Aw, you must be proud of him. Do you see much of him?
B: Not really. He's busy. That's how it goes.
A: Yeah. My mum says the same about me, and I'm ten minutes away. I still feel guilty. Sorry, I'm rambling. Do you do anything outside work?
B: Not much. Surveys. These. Pub quiz now and then if the wife drags me.
A: Oh, pub quiz! I do one every week, I'm the history and sport man. We came second last week by one point. One point, Gary. It was a question on the Tudors and I got it wrong. I'm meant to be the Tudors man.
B: I'm the telly one. Quiz shows, Only Fools. Can't do the music round.
A: Nobody can do the music round. It's always some band from 1983 nobody's heard of.
B: Pays out on the meat raffle, ours. That's the only reason I go.
A: Ha, a meat raffle! Now that's a proper prize. What did you win?
B: Leg of lamb once. Tracey done it for Sunday dinner. Best thing I ever won.
A: Best thing he ever won. A leg of lamb. Honestly, that's lovely. My dad won a—
